utterances.text: I think the existence of trenches is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in your neighborhood, did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: No. No, not in the area where I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them outside that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: I did, yes, when I left -- when I went out of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you see people working at those trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: I used to see people working at those trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us, what do you know, who were those people? Were they military or were they civilians, to your knowledge, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: They were civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us a little bit more, that is, according to you, were they -- could it be a construction company that had sent its workers or was it perhaps some other system at work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: They were just rank and file citizens who were rounded up in streets or summoned directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you say that they were rounded up in the streets. Who did that? Who rounded them up in the streets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: In the area which I covered when going to work, those areas or parts of them would quite often be blocked and the people had to show their IDs, their papers. And it was the basis on which they selected people who would have to go and dig trenches. I was intercepted three times -- I was stopped on three occasions by women and told not to go into the streets that had been blocked, so as not to find myself in that situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I don't quite understand what you are saying. Is it your capacity to dig something that you can read from your identity card or why, for instance, this request to show your papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well, they were checking your ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the consequences of this? What is the conclusion that can be drawn from it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well, since the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was basically made of Muslims, then the trench diggers ought to have been Serbs, by and large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand your testimony well, you are telling us that the authorities were collecting -- were making the screening of civilians so as to when they were Serbs they would send them to the front lines, is that what you are trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And would there be fighting when people were sent like that to work on the front lines; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Yes. And the fighting would erupt all of a sudden, unexpectedly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness how did the authorities react if somebody was stopped, but then said "I don't want to go and dig trenches," to your knowledge, what was their reaction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: I don't think that could happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well, you would simply be apprehended, put in a van or a truck and taken to the place where you were supposed to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to describe to us a kind of campaign intended to provide labour which would -- who would be forced to go to the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well it looked like forced labour, and I guess it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, does -- did it seem to you structured, organised, I mean, either from the point of view of -- by administration or by the military.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: In the area where I used to go through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is the third leading question that my learned colleague has put to the witness. The previous two put to the witness where he had not previously said it, that the trenches were on the front line. So these are not technical leading questions. I respectfully submit to you that the Defence should not ask leading questions on such critical issues in chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it is my recollection that the witness testified that he saw trenches when he left the city. That is as far as the location is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is quite true, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But did he say it was at the front lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that he said so, but we can clarify it. However, I am going to ask him whether it was under fire or under shells and he said "yes." But I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these trenches, did they -- did they follow the front line, that is, were they at the confrontation line between the two camps?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that also is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where -- all right. Let me put it this way: Where were those trenches?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the question by itself is without any relevance. The question should be placed in a context, that is, which trenches, and perhaps an appropriate starting point of the trenches that this witness is forced to dig, where were those trenches?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is -- let's keep it as factual as possible, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Let's not ask where trenches were in Sarajevo, but let's -- could you please try to put your questions in such a way that we get the information from the witness which comes from his own experience and his own observation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these trenches that we are talking about, could you -- could you locate them? Could you place them so that we can see? Could you somehow look at them in space so that we would know where they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that question also does not given an appropriate context. The trenches that we are talking about, what trenches, in what context? Trenches that this witness dug, that he saw other people that he knew to be Serb civilians digging or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can ask a question which can be very very long and I think it is much better if I asked him -- if request ask it in three stages, in three steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to be as factual as possible in your questioning, so that we could, first of all, get the answers concerning facts known to the witness. So would you please be very precise in asking for facts rather than general. Perhaps, first ask whether he saw trenches. He answered that question already. But when he saw then, whether he had to dig them, whether he knew of anyone else. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell the Chamber at what time did you see trenches, what type of them, in relation to the work performed by civilians there or at them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: I saw trenches. I already said when I went out of Sarajevo travelling in the cabin of a truck I could see trenches in two places. One as you come out of Stupska Petlja and then on another occasion as coming down from Trebevic, I could see on one side there were trenches. I mentioned those two names, and I won't mention them again. But one of them worked in the early days at the Jewish cemetery, that is where the confrontation line. And another friend dug at Trebevic and at the foot hill --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness please repeat the other place name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... repetez les deux dernier noms de lieus que vous avez indiquez. Je crois que vous avez dit, Cimetiere Juif et l'autre? Pour raison de traduction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: The line along Trebevic, and a second at Poljine and that is what these people told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, thank you, Witness. Now, in relation to those men to those people that you just mentioned did -- or this man, did he go to those places of his own will; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: No. One of them was a very sick man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it one of those people who were just rounded up in the street indiscriminately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well, that could be true of one of them. As for the other one, well, they came to his home and summoned him to go and dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you said that if this task was not accepted by people, then these people would be taken somewhere in a lorry. Is this what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you were taken somewhere in a lorry towards which direction was it? For instance, was it a prison? I am not saying anything, I am not implying anything, but why would one be taken in a lorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the question still does not follow the proper form. Essentially it is an invitation to speculate. It is not a specific request for information which is within the witness's knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Mr. President, that the witness said that if you didn't accept to go, then you were still taken in a lorry. So what I am to know, what I am interested in, is whether the witness knows what would happen, or what would have happened after someone was taken in a lorry. And that is this type of question that I would like to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you in fact, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you should ask the witness whether he ever observed such a lorry, and in what direction it drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, with pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I further say that the question where you second sentence was "I am not implying anything," you were leading in an unacceptable way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should also add now that I have had an opportunity to check, that according to my search of LiveNote. The witness has not referred to a lorry at all. I think the witness said they were taken anyway, which does not lend itself to the interpretation of Mr. Piletta-Zanin that they were taken somewhere different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it was a lorry or not, it is my recollection, true or not, and I am also looking to my colleagues that there was some means of transportation the witness was referring to. But I can check that, and looking in the LiveNote for the word lorry might make you miss a similar form of transportation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, specifically, did you know of situations where people would have refused to go and dig?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: I know of one case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, therefore, tell us what happened in this case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: He spent a night in Trebevic. He found some people that he knew up there and those people pulled some strings who knew some people who were high-ranking, and he managed to get back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a person who was perhaps sick or something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has not said that this person was sick or something else. The question, yet again offends the rules of examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it is my recollection that the witness testified that one of the two persons he knew about was sick or something like that. So you should first verify whether this was one of the persons and whether it was the sick person or the person that he did not call to be sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke of these two cases, and in one of these cases a person was sick; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The person that you just spoke of earlier, was it this sick person that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: This is a third person who was not sick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Which one was not sick?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Those two out of whom one was sick kept on digging trenches, and I told you that one who had refused to dig trenches, he was put on a lorry, he was taken to Mount Trebevic. He spent the night there, among the soldiers there. He either found an acquaintance or an acquaintance of an acquaintance and there was a quick intervention of some influential people from Sarajevo, and he was returned to Trebevic to his employment. At the moment he is a high-ranking official in the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you say that he spent the night in Mount Trebevic, what do you mean by that? Is there something specific that you have in mind? For us, it is an area, I believe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well apart from the trenches, there was certainly, there was the troops, there were shelters for the army, huts. I presume that is where he could have spent the night. It is an acquaintance of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know -- I am going to rephrase my question. Let us imagine that during the period that we know about, the period of the war, somebody does something which is contrary to the law, something that is illegal, and this person in your area, in your neighborhood, would have been a -- who would have been in charge of police in your area, in your neighborhood, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: As far as my personal experience goes, all of the communications, although it was not in relation to illegal actions, this was done by members of the police or the measures were undertaken by the members of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said, and I am going to try to quote you in relation to the transcript, but in relation to my personal experience or as far as my personal experience goes, what are you saying about that? Are you talking about a personal experience, something that you have experienced yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was this personal experience that you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: There are a few but my first experience with the police in terms of being detained, that was in October 1992 when members of police force came for me to hand me over to the Military Police in Viktor Bubanj, and I was charged, I was accused of having betrayed, having committed the act of treason because I changed the place of residence and therefore avoided receiving the call up papers for the regular Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and, therefore, I put at risk the independent sovereignty and so on of the state. Of course I was at the address which I hadn't changed for 10 years and still I found myself in the prison in Viktor Bubanj. And thanks to the police who brought me there, I stayed only one day, because they tried to find a military judge because I was found on the actual scene, I had all the documents, and the military judge ruled that I had not committed the -- what I had been charged with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that this happened on one occasion, and I believe that you said in your language that this was the first time, but I am not able to follow everything on the transcript. But was it the only time, the one time that you were confronted to this type of situations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you about it, but reluctantly so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why are you hesitating to answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: There was several pointless summons, detentions, interrogations, accusations. I truly believed that if there had only been one tiny detail that was true in all these accusations, I certainly would not have been sitting here today as a witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps I can assist you in a sense that I can see you becoming emotional. Were you arrested on several occasions by this police force or Military Police force or whatever police we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object on the grounds of leading, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I know, I am aware that this is a leading question. I thought that this would not be objected to because I can see the emotion of the witness. I will remember that. I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, one would have thought that a prerequisite to not expecting an objection would be to have referred to this evidence, whatever it is, in the description of the evidence which is anticipated from the witness, and I don't recollect anything of this nature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke once that you were arrested. Could you please, in the interest of justice, could you please tell us more about it, if there are -- if there is more to say about the subject.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: Well, at one point I was detained, accused of, so to speak, that I was accused of participating in ethnic cleansing. Because, as an activist of Dobrocinstvo, I was helping people to leave with the approval and the order, and then they would leave and then they wouldn't come back. Now, the second time it was a more serious accusation. I was accused of participating with some people in an act of creating a kind of enemy centre out of this humanitarian association that I was calling people to establish some kind of sabotage, subversive group, which was supposed to cause an incident or even bloodshed in Sarajevo, so that Serb crimes would then be diverted so that the attention would be diverted from the Serb crimes and I was then taken for interrogation. And at the end when there was nothing else left, I was even accused, I was even charged with, there was proceedings that was initiated against me, I was charged that with as a member of the humanitarian organisation, I have committed the misuse, abuse of my position that a company that was doing us a favour by giving -- lending us lorries because the humanitarian association Benefactor did not have its own lorries, so they had to be borrowed and they had to be paid for. And I claim before this Chamber that -- I claim that not one parcel or one kilo, kilogram, of food was distributed without the approval and the permission of the then-financial police. However, I was detained and I was interrogated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This will be my --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this will be my very last question

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard you saying in French that this was your very last question. You said before the break a few minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that not a single parcel went out of the way, that every single parcel was delivered, and we don't doubt it, but the distribution of aids that you were involved with, what was it like? Was it equitable, was it selective, destined to only some categories of the population? What can you tell us about this, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP1
utterances.text: When we are talking about family parcels, they arrived at the address of all citizens, regardless of their ethic or religious belonging. They normally came from Yugoslavia. Of course, the most important number came to Serb addresses, but there was a high percentage of Croats or Muslims who had friends or relatives in Yugoslavia. And you know that there are many people who have relations in Belgrade and Muslims in Belgrade and Muslims in Sandzak and in Sarajevo. So this is as for the family parcels that went to the addresses and this was checked by the police which is natural. And because there were some central points where these parcels arrived and these policemen were, and we had excellent cooperation with them I have to say, we were aware of the situation we were in and we had no problems with that. And I have already told the Chamber we had little humanitarian aid except for two occasions. Once one humanitarian association -- the only association that we had a completely equitable relationship or relation to attitude to all the ethnic groups which was called Baltimor [phoen] a Catholic association. On one occasion they gave us 25 pounds of sugar. Because there was no regular supply, we wanted to have a global distribution to the population. So we distributed this according to the list that we had at points, and this was distributed to Serb families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP1, this concludes the examination-in-chief where the transcript, by mistake says that you were cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but you will now be examined by the Prosecution. Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I indicate, that since you asked for some time, that you would stop at anything between 10 and 8 minutes to 7.00, because it might take a bit more time and we might even have to go in closed session for the guidance you are seeking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, the witness was shown a map which I don't think at this stage has an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1755 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown the map and it may be appropriate for the questions to be dealt with in closed session. It shouldn't take more than a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We then turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.04 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of October, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
